pass_condition: A migration that fails partway leaves the database exactly as it was before the call.

findings.statement: A failed migration is not rolled back: conn.executescript() commits the pending transaction first, so the v1 rename and every statement before the failure are already durable.
findings.failure_scenario: On a copy of the real v1 DB, a syntax error in the middle of 0001 leaves the DB with legacy_repositories (rename committed), a NEW EMPTY repositories table and no schema_migrations row: 'A: rows now reachable as repositories: 0'. Every v1 reader of that database now sees zero rows. With a later migration (0002) failing, 'later_ok' from the failed migration stays committed and 0002 is unrecorded, so re-running it fails permanently on CREATE TABLE later_ok.

observations: The docstring claims the opposite -- 'Commits once at the end so a partial failure leaves the database at its pre-call state under SQLite's default transactional DDL' -- an untrue docstring (L2-06).
Fix: run each statement of the file inside one explicit BEGIN ... COMMIT with rollback() on exception, instead of executescript().

not_checked.statement: W4-3's persona re-projection SQL and W4-4's endpoints are not in this packet; only the reader helpers they build on were checked.
